transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick check - can you all hear me?
[00:05] Carlos (Aptiva): Yep loud and clear.
[00:10] Jordan: Awesome. We're on for 45 minutes, agenda - quick results recap, dive into p95/p99 variance, quantization notes from Priya, and propose next steps. Priya will lead the technical bits.
[00:25] Priya (Redwood SE): Hi team. So slide 1 - recapping the bench we ran last week vs the baseline provider you shared. We normalized to the same request mix, 200 token avg, and your 50 req/s sustained profile. Redwood numbers are here: p50 22ms, p95 120ms, p99 210ms on our hosted instance using the optimized kernel path. Throughput scaled to ~115 qps with batching window tuned.
[00:47] Sara (Aptiva): Wait you said 22ms p50? that feels low compared to what we're seeing from BaselineCloud. Baseline reported p50 28ms, p95 180, p99 350. Is that apples to apples?
[01:00] Priya: Good question. We matched model size and sequence len, but the baseline run didn't enable prefix KV cache or continuous batching. once you enable KV cache you should see the big gains on repeat context. Our p95 gap vs baseline is largely the KV cache + optimized kernels + slightly better batching.
[01:18] Liam (CTO): Can you explain the KV cache difference - is that a Redwood-only feature or standard?
[01:25] Priya: It's standard in modern runtimes but our implementation keeps cache hot across concurrent sessions with a small eviction policy tuned for your workload. there was a small discrepancy in their run - in their notes they called it "KV cash" which I think is a transcribe error, but they weren't warming cache between bursts. that increases tail latency.
[01:45] Jordan: Also worth noting we ran the quantized variant (4-bit) for one of the tests - gives ~2.1x throughput improvement but p99 tail stretches if memory spill occurs. Priya, can you walk the tradeoffs?
[01:59] Priya: Sure. Quantization (we tested int4 + GPTQ style) reduces memory and increases throughput; on dedicated GPU pools you get predictable latency. on hosted there's more scheduler variability but still net gain. downside: off-nominal sequences and very long contexts can trigger dequantization slow paths and you see p99 spikes. Our recommendation: use quantized for bulk inference with prefix caching and fall back to fp16 for critical low-tail requests.
[02:26] Carlos: That's helpful; our main concern is p99 for billing queries — if a small percentage of requests trip dequantization and cost triple we need mitigation.
[02:35] Priya: Mitigation options: 1) keep a hybrid pool - quantized for bulk, fp16 fallback for high-SLA calls; 2) set routing policy to avoid burst co-location; 3) enable proactive KV warming for the most common prefixes. We can provide an SLO-based routing config.
[02:53] Sara: About the throughput - you mentioned 115 qps; our baseline peaked at 98 qps under the same concurrency. can you share the raw traces?
[03:02] Jordan: We'll send the spreadsheet with raw traces, p50/p95/p99 columns, and the actual request timestamps. expect that in an email after the call.
[03:10] Priya: Quick note on how we measure - we include kernel stalls and context switch delays. BaselineCloud's public numbers may have filtered some infra jitter.
[03:20] Liam: Ok. on the Dedicated vs hosted decision - if we go Dedicated what are the guarantees?
[03:27] Jordan: Dedicated (reserved) gives you predictable throughput and isolation. SLA-backed uptime and latency targets, configurable autoscaling, and you can pin model versions. We'll send a 4x A100-equivalent quote based on your sustained 50 req/s profile and desired headroom.
[03:44] Carlos: And Private? We might need a VPC/on-prem for compliance. you have an on-prem package with KMS integration right?
[03:50] Jordan: Yes, Redwood Private supports customer-managed networking, KMS/HSM, and audit logs. we'll include SOC2 and KMS docs.
[03:58] Sara: About audit logs - we need sample retention policies and how long trace data lives in the host. also SAML/SSO integration for RBAC.
[04:08] Priya: We'll attach a security pack; it includes retention options, SSO/SAML notes, RBAC patterns, and HIPAA-adjacent controls we've seen customers ask for.
[04:18] Jordan: Back to the bench: there was one run where p99 spiked to ~480ms during a background compaction event. Priya, do you recall that?
[04:25] Priya: Yeah that was on the fp16 run with GC + kernel recompile causing a stall. we flagged it. in dedicated infra those jitter events are much rarer since we avoid noisy neighbors.
[04:35] Carlos: Can you reproduce that with our traffic mix?
[04:38] Priya: We can - next step is a 24h soak using your traffic profile on your infra to capture long-tail events. request we get the sample mix.
[04:46] Jordan: Carlos, can you share the traffic profile?
[04:48] Carlos: I'll export and send the 90-day slice; it's about 62% short queries (<50 tokens), 28% medium (50-250), 10% long. I'll send by Monday.
[04:57] Sara: On the integration side, how invasive is the SDK? we prefer minimal changes.
[05:02] Priya: Two options - lightweight REST calls with streaming or our SDK which has built-in batching and KV helpers. the SDK reduces client-side complexity and gives you better batching behavior.
[05:12] Liam: Any gotchas on TLS/KMS?
[05:15] Jordan: We support customer KMS for Private, and hosted connections encrypt in transit. SSO/SAML is supported for console access; for API keys you can integrate with our keystore. we'll include the specifics in the security pack.
[05:28] Carlos: Competitors - baselinecloud seems to underperform tails but cheaper at list price. how does Redwood's unit economics stack?
[05:36] Jordan: Redwood Optimize has cost/perf recommendations — we can run an estimate for your mix. quantization + batching + prefix cache typically reduces token cost by 30-50%. we'll include a modeled cost comparison vs BaselineCloud and an in-house estimate.
[05:49] Priya: One more technical detail: your current baseline used a slightly different tokenizer (their preproc trims max context). that changes the effective token count and can bias throughput. we normalized for that but wanted you to be aware.
[06:03] Sara: Ok. Any infra prerequisites for the soak?
[06:06] Priya: For the on-prem soak, we'll need VPC info, a peering endpoint or jump host, and a small test account. Sara, you mentioned VPC peering checklist - if you share region and egress rules we'll draft the exact steps.
[06:21] Sara: We'll do that.
[06:23] Jordan: Quick note on monitoring - console will show per-route latency breakdown and token-level cost. we'll grant you a demo tenant if you want to explore more dashboards.
[06:33] Carlos: Great. I also want the raw traces to run our own p99 analysis and maybe feed to our APM. format?
[06:38] Priya: CSV with timestamp, latency_ms, model_variant, node_id, and a small sample of request context. we'll send that.
[06:45] Liam: On the fallback logic - can Redwood route to a cheaper model if latency grows?
[06:50] Jordan: Yes, smart routing supports policy-based fallback to cheaper variants or other regions. can do cost-based or latency-based policies.
[06:58] Sara: A question on billing - if we do Dedicated but run a mix of quantized and fp16, how is billing metered?
[07:04] Jordan: Dedicated is generally capacity-based (reserved nodes) plus optional per-token adjustments for premium fp16 usage. we'll detail in the pricing doc.
[07:12] Priya: also on the technical side, please note inference kernels choose execution path based on sequence length distribution; very long sequences sometimes pick slower kernels. warming short prefixes helps.
[07:25] Carlos: Any idea how many tokens before dequantization triggers?
[07:28] Priya: It's more about sequence complexity and memory pressure than a hard token count - but for your mix it was around sequences >900 tokens that started to see dequantization slow paths.
[07:38] Jordan: Ok let's capture concrete next steps. we'll: 1) send benchmark spreadsheet and raw traces, 2) Priya runs 24h soak on quantized & fp16 using Carlos's traffic, 3) Jordan sends Dedicated quote + security pack, 4) schedule follow-up on 2026-10-08.
[07:55] Carlos: Sounds good. One small ask - can you include an estimated ops lift for Private deployment? we want to understand runbook/work effort.
[08:03] Jordan: We'll add an ops estimate and on-prem package outline.
[08:08] Liam: Thanks — also include rollback plan for model changes.
[08:12] Priya: We'll include canary rollout options and automatic fallback policies in the doc.
[08:18] Jordan: Any final questions?
[08:20] Sara: None from me.
[08:22] Carlos: No. thanks.
[08:24] Jordan: Great, we'll follow up by EOD tomorrow with the spreadsheet and security pack and get the soak scheduled once we have the traffic. Thanks everyone.
[08:32] (call ends)
